# Add marginal distribution plots to a scatter plot

Draws the distribution of the plotted X values in a strip above a
single-panel plotly figure, and of the Y values in a strip to its right,
as a density curve, a histogram, a rug, or any combination of them. One
trace is drawn per group, in that group's colour, and the rug gives each
group its own lane so groups do not overplot.

## Usage

``` r
add_marginal_plots(
  fig,
  x,
  y,
  groups = NULL,
  colors = "#000000",
  top = character(0),
  right = character(0),
  top.size = 0.15,
  right.size = 0.15,
  opacity = 0.5,
  bins = 30,
  binwidth = NULL,
  density.adjust = 1,
  rug.size = 0.3,
  rug.length = 0.8,
  rug.width = 1,
  gap = 0.02
)
```

## Arguments

- fig:

  A single-panel plotly figure.

- x, y:

  Numeric vectors of the plotted X and Y values, one per point. Pass the
  values as drawn (after any data adjustment), not the raw data.
  Non-finite values are dropped.

- groups:

  A vector or factor of the same length giving each point's group, or
  `NULL` for a single ungrouped distribution. Factor levels set the
  order of the rug lanes.

- colors:

  Colours for the groups: a vector named by group, or an unnamed vector
  recycled over the groups in level order. Without groups, the first
  colour is used.

- top, right:

  Character vectors of the marginals to draw above the plot (for `x`)
  and to its right (for `y`), any of `"density"`, `"histogram"` and
  `"rug"`. An empty vector draws nothing on that side.

- top.size, right.size:

  Fraction of the plot's height (`top.size`) or width (`right.size`)
  given to that side's marginals, from 0.02 to 0.8.

- opacity:

  Opacity of the density and histogram fills and of the rug lines, 0 to
  1.

- bins:

  Number of histogram bins, spanning the range of all groups' values.

- binwidth:

  Histogram bin width. When given, it overrides `bins`, and the bins are
  aligned to multiples of it.

- density.adjust:

  Multiplier on the density bandwidth, as `adjust` in
  [`stats::density()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/density.html). Larger
  values smooth more.

- rug.size:

  Share of a side's strip given to the rug when the side also has a
  density or histogram, 0.1 to 0.9. A rug on its own fills the side.

- rug.length:

  Length of each rug tick as a fraction of its group's lane, 0 to 1.

- rug.width:

  Line width of the rug ticks, in pixels.

- gap:

  Paper-space gap between the main panel and the marginals.

## Value

The built plotly figure with the marginals added, or `fig` unchanged
when `top` and `right` are both empty.

## Details

The main panel is shrunk to make room, and each strip's value axis
`matches` the main axis, so zooming or panning the plot moves its
marginals with it. Paper-anchored shapes (such as the panel border
ggplotly draws) and axis-title annotations from
[`axis_titles_as_annotations()`](https://j-andrews7.github.io/VizModules/reference/axis_titles_as_annotations.md)
are moved into the shrunk panel.

Call this last, once everything else has been drawn: helpers that work
per panel (fit lines, reference lines, axis styling) read the strips'
extra axes as facet panels. It is not meant for a faceted figure.

A density and a histogram on the same side share one strip, the
histogram drawn first and scaled to a density (count / (n \* bin width))
so both share a scale; a histogram on its own shows counts. A rug sits
in a strip of its own, between the main panel and any density or
histogram. Densities, like ggplot2's, span each group's range of values.
Every marginal is a line trace, so box and lasso selection pick only the
plot's points, and each takes its group's `legendgroup`, so hiding a
group from the legend hides its marginals too.

## See also

[`stats::density()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/density.html),
[`axis_titles_as_annotations()`](https://j-andrews7.github.io/VizModules/reference/axis_titles_as_annotations.md)

## Author

Jared Andrews

## Examples

``` r
library(plotly)
df <- example_iris
fig <- plot_ly(df,
    x = ~Sepal.Length, y = ~Sepal.Width, color = ~Species,
    type = "scatter", mode = "markers"
)
add_marginal_plots(fig,
    x = df$Sepal.Length, y = df$Sepal.Width, groups = df$Species,
    colors = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73"),
    top = c("density", "rug"), right = "histogram"
)
```
